optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Collaboration Software Subscriptions

professionalSummary.text: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self-service billing pages.
professionalSummary.witness: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self-service billing pages.

experienceHighlights.text: Turned weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories with acceptance criteria for self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages.
experienceHighlights.witness: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.

experienceHighlights.text: Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging passed and failed criteria.
experienceHighlights.witness: Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.

experienceHighlights.text: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with engineering manager and subscription operations lead, with scope and release date being the engineering manager's call.
experienceHighlights.witness: Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

experienceHighlights.text: Published release notes for seat-change and invoice-download pages detailing one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and support team handover requirements.
experienceHighlights.witness: Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Work sample includes story set for invoice-download page with acceptance criteria and pass/fail log from one acceptance session, with ticket identifiers for traceability.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the story set for the invoice-download page with its acceptance criteria, plus the pass/fail log from one acceptance session; ticket identifiers are included so the entries can be traced.

skills.text: Self-service billing and seat-management page requirements gathering, user story writing, acceptance testing, and release notes publication.
skills.witness: Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self-service billing pages.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's experience with intake, story writing, acceptance sessions, release notes, and work samples for the self-service billing pages, but do not establish any reduction in billing support tickets as measured against a baseline.

decisionBoundary.statement: Human review required to assess whether the candidate's work reduced billing support tickets as measured against a baseline.

role.roleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Collaboration Software Subscriptions

evidence.text: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.
Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.

candidate said billing tickets 'fell by about 30 percent' after the invoice-download page launched; he said the support team had mentioned it in a stand-up and that he had not seen a ticket report himself.
Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

supportedClaims.witness: Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.

unsupportedClaims.claim: Billing tickets fell by about 30 percent after the invoice-download page launched.
unsupportedClaims.reason: The candidate's statement is hearsay and not documented; the support team mentioned it in a stand-up, but the candidate did not see a ticket report.
unsupportedClaims.requiredFollowUp: Ask for the documented baseline, metric definition, observation window, and concurrent changes.

interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Ask for documented metric, baseline, observation window, and concurrent changes.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you provide the documented baseline for billing support tickets before and after the invoice-download page launch, including the metric definition, observation window, and any concurrent changes that might have affected the metric?

limitations: The candidate's statement about ticket reduction is hearsay and not documented; no baseline data is provided in the sources.
